dedupNotes: PATTERN-001 (REENTRANCY-ERC777 pattern, potential-high): exact duplicate of CODE-001's mechanism (ERC1155 receiver callback mid-loop, no guard). Folded in — same contract:function:rootCauseClass.

SLITHER-001 (reentrancy-events, L284, potential-low): corroborating static signal (NudgePaid emitted after external calls, no nonReentrant). Tool-grade; same root cause. Folded in as corroboration, not a separate finding.

ECON-004 (informational): economic-lens restatement of the same reentrancy surface; explicitly defers to profile LOCAL-002 and concludes the NUDGE-POT leg is not double-spendable. Folded in — it corroborates the negative result on the pot leg but does NOT cover the payment-refund leg that CODE-001 newly identifies.
Aderyn HIGH reentrancy at NFTStaker.sol:445 was already excluded by the static scanner as out-of-scopeFocus (context contract, not the story-015 change) — not carried.
deduplicatedFindings.novelInsightVsL01: L-01 was adjudicated NOT-exploitable because the analysis treated every value-out path as balanceOf-driven and idempotent-to-zero (true for the NUDGE POT: first safeTransfer zeroes it, a re-entrant qualifying batch reads 0). CODE-001 identifies a DIFFERENT, non-idempotent value-out path the prior adjudication did not analyse: the PAYMENT-TOKEN dust refund at L287-289 sweeps the whole live balanceOf(this) to the CURRENT frame's msg.sender. A re-entrant inner frame's sweep therefore pays out the OUTER (victim) frame's still-unspent paymentAmount to the attacker. This is the concrete third-party value-extraction path that was missing from L-01, and it is what would justify escalation Low -> High.
exploitabilityCaveats: Requires a non-attacker balance to be present in the contract at callback time, i.e. an honest caller's in-flight paymentAmount or an externally pre-funded balance. If every caller mints only to their own EOA and no third party pre-loads value, the attacker only churns their own funds (self-pay, no theft).

CODE-001's cited realistic trigger is the integration context: BalancerPoolerV2 (story-031) pushing USDC into a batchMinter address, and front-ends batching mints to arbitrary recipient contracts. That integration assumption lives OUTSIDE this submodule and must be validated for the High to stand — otherwise this is the defense-in-depth Low as originally filed.

Severity is 'potential-high' in the source scan and MUST be treated as escalation-CANDIDATE only until a Tier-3 PoC demonstrates cross-party extraction with a realistic deployment config (nudge funded, victim batch whose recipient is a contract). Absent that PoC, the validated state remains L-01 Low.

C4 note: if the only way to place a third party's funds in the contract is the out-of-submodule BalancerPoolerV2 integration, confirm the root cause is in-scope (the missing guard IS in this contract) and that the funding pattern is not a user-input/integration mistake on the known-invalid list.
deduplicatedFindings.recommendation: Add OZ ReentrancyGuard and mark batchMint nonReentrant (parity with sibling NFTStaker, which guards every entrypoint). This closes the entire class regardless of whether the High exploitability holds. Cheap and decisive.

deduplicatedFindings.recommendation: Per ECON-001: a slippage floor cannot fix a winner-take-all race because the value is binary and fully visible. Design-level fix needed — (a) per-qualifying-mint pull-style accrual, (b) cap per-call payout to a fixed amount rather than sweeping balanceOf, or (c) commit-reveal/auction settlement. At minimum, re-document M-01 as a known accepted MEV exposure rather than 'resolved'.

ledgerDecisionDetail.question: Is CODE-001 the SAME finding as ledger L-01 (escalated), or a DISTINCT new finding?
ledgerDecisionDetail.answer: SAME finding as L-01, re-adjudicated and escalated. NOT a new/distinct finding.
reasoning: Identical mechanical root cause: batchMint has no nonReentrant guard, and the ERC1155 onERC1155Received mint hook (fired by nftMinter.mint to a caller-chosen recipient mid-loop) hands control to attacker code while paymentAmount is held and max approval is live. L-01, CODE-001, PATTERN-001 and SLITHER-001 all describe this one defect.

The ledger fingerprint scheme keys on contract:function:rootCauseClass. I verified sha256('src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:batchMint:missing-reentrancy-guard') reproduces L-01's stored fingerprint 9135cf... byte-for-byte. CODE-001 maps to the identical tuple, so it MUST reuse that fingerprint or it would create a ledger duplicate of an already-open finding.

What changed is the SEVERITY ADJUDICATION, not the finding. L-01 was filed Low (defense-in-depth) because the prior run concluded no reentrant frame could extract third-party value. That conclusion was reached by analysing the nudge-pot leg (correctly idempotent-to-zero). CODE-001 supplies the missing piece: the payment-token dust-refund sweep (L287-289) is NOT idempotent across frames — it pays balanceOf(this) to the current frame's msg.sender, so a re-entrant inner frame can carry an outer victim's paymentAmount out to the attacker. That is a new exploitability insight on the SAME root cause, i.e. an escalation.

Per the deduplicator rules: 'Same vulnerability pattern with same root cause' => consolidate, and 'Conflicting Severity: Preserve highest severity instance.' Treating CODE-001 as a new finding would double-report the same contract:function:rootCauseClass and split the ledger history of an open submission.

Operationally this is a REOPEN + RE-CLASSIFY of L-01: L-01 is currently status=submitted at Low. The finding-manager should keep fingerprint 9135cf..., update severity Low -> High (or High-candidate), append the CODE-001 payment-refund exploit path as the new exploitability evidence, and bump lastSeenRun to phoenix-nft-staking-14. Because the prior run DELIBERATELY adjudicated this NOT-exploitable, the severity flip is gated on a Tier-3 PoC and is flagged for human review (humanReviewFlag on DEDUP-001).
ledgerDecisionDetail.notARegression: Not a REGRESSION in the ledger sense: L-01 was never marked fixed (status=submitted). The escalation is new analysis on an open finding, not the reappearance of a fixed one.
